verdict: PASS. All four bars met on evidence I gathered myself, on a private instance, with the repository unchanged by the measurement.

stopwatch.story: JS-16, the model steward decides whether to ship
stopwatch.baseline: cannot start: zero of the 113 published operations were training, the gate table lived on the operator's Events calendar, and there was no model version identity
stopwatch.note: app time about 9.5 s end to end, of which 9.1 s is the audience training run itself (exit 0, 7.9 s of process). Reading thirteen gate cards is the only human cost and every one of them is on the first screen.

ab.reference: TensorBoard 2.18.0, launched by me on my own port over three scalar runs written for the comparison
ab.result: Meridian wins on every mechanic JS-16 needs. The reference surface contains no gate, no bar, no reason, no control that starts a run and no way to record a ship or no-ship verdict against a named version; run identity is a directory name a human typed, against a content digest here. TensorBoard wins only on interactive curve exploration (smoothing, zoom, pinned overlay), which a five-point weekly drift series does not need.
ab.note: traffica.base44.app remains unreachable, the Chrome extension is still not connected, so no comparison against the trade reference was invented.

regression.tests: 105 tests under the test_p7_ prefix pass, measured in two runs (38 then 67). Matches the count P7 claims.
regression.gate_coverage: all 8 gates in models/audience_model.json and all 5 retention gate families are in the ledger, so nothing the Events calendar used to show is missing
regression.impact_route: GET /api/impact still answers a channel account 200 with state unavailable and an honest Hebrew reason rather than a 403, so the operator surface that consumes it is not broken
regression.repository: models/releases/training_runs.json and decisions.jsonl md5 identical before and after my run; both stores were relocated to scratch for the measurement

laws.honest_math: two figures traced byte for byte to the artifacts: retention.first_break p=0.20341935034834022 with n 476 first and 816 later, and audience.competitor_lineup held_out_delta_pct=2.162518438605128
laws.competitor_boundary: zero rival channel names across all eight console payloads; coverage says four channels are in the base and names only the operator's own, with the sentence that non-operator channels are counted and never named
laws.training_versus_runs: every model route 403s for a channel account, the switcher does not render for one, and the console's own runs write only into the releases store, never over models/tv_break_coefficients.json
laws.characters_and_size: zero em-dashes, en-dashes, emojis or exclamation marks and no file over 450 lines across every P7-owned source and test
laws.vocabulary: the only hits for the forbidden noun are the verb form in 'the runs use it', not the noun

largest_gap: The decision path is the one write on this console whose affordance does not tell the truth before the click, and the one screen that makes a claim its own behaviour does not back. POST /api/model/decisions is not stamped with can_edit, so a company viewer sees an enabled Record control while both Train buttons are already disabled with the wall's Hebrew refusal; and the refusal that actually lands is the English 'A viewer session is read-only.' from kairos_api/auth.py:111, not the Hebrew sentence the console promises, which tests/test_p7_can_edit.py cannot catch because it compares the stamp to MODEL_WALL.reason() rather than to the write route's real body. In the same file, VersionsPanel.jsx's header comment claims the form says a ship verdict copies no artifact; measured on screen it says no such thing, and a recorded ship verdict on the current model renders the single word 'Shipped' with no qualifier, because DecisionRow prints an adoption line only when the state is 'escalated'.
minor: the four header count chips are plain spans while the same four counts one screen below are working filters, so a number in the header opens nothing

the console never says that placebo_correction_active and interval_calibration are method defaults rather than gates, which is why the ledger is 13 and not 15; provenance shows the placebo seed but neither the switch nor its reason

console-words.js packs the English and Hebrew strings of an entry on one source line where the frozen vocabulary.js gives each its own; src/sources does the same, so this is a convention split across the wave rather than a P7 defect
measurement_hazard_for_the_next_agent: Every server on 127.0.0.1 shares one cookie jar with every other port, and the shared Chrome tab group is being navigated by six other agents. A reading taken across two calls can mix two accounts: one of mine looked exactly like the console header lying about permission and was not. Measure over http://[::1]:8085 in a tab you created, guard every evaluate on location.origin, and take identity and screen in the same call.
